::: {#exm-marginal-likelihood}
#### Posterior probability that a coin is biased, computed

Continuing @exm-posterior,
let $\vy$ be the three heads,
so $\p(\vy \mid \param) = \param^3$.
The [marginal likelihood](#def-marginal-likelihood) sums over the two possible values of $\param$:

$$
\ba
\p(\vy)
&= \p(\vy \mid 0.5)\, \p(0.5) + \p(\vy \mid 0.8)\, \p(0.8)\\
&= 0.5^3 \cdot 0.9 + 0.8^3 \cdot 0.1\\
&= 0.1125 + 0.0512\\
&= 0.1637.
\ea
$$

By @thm-bayes-posterior,

$$
\p(0.8 \mid \vy)
= \frac{\p(\vy \mid 0.8)\, \p(0.8)}{\p(\vy)}
= \frac{0.0512}{0.1637}
\approx 0.313,
$$

and $\p(0.5 \mid \vy) = 0.1125 / 0.1637 \approx 0.687$.
Three heads in a row raise the probability that the coin is biased
from $0.1$ to about $0.31$.
:::
